# Source artifact inventory for distributed and concurrent problems
(authored by agents unless marked 🧑)

- scope
  - source-only inventory of 1,546 files/directories, not 1,546 verified protocols
  - rows distinguish stated properties, proof text and recorded checking; no verification tools were run here
  - source repositories inspected on 6–7 October 2026; GitHub links pin inspected commits; author bundles use dated source URLs
  - 1,546 source-artifact rows, grouped by tool; variants, encodings, proof modules, model instances and named clients can have separate rows
  - row count includes supporting artifacts; distinct algorithms are not counted; coverage and unlocated sources are recorded below
  - each row records the modeled problem, separate safety/liveness evidence, tool/status, physical source lines and exact source link
  - 78 GitHub repository roots represented by pinned links, plus author source bundles
  - link audit: 4,920 unique commit-pinned file/directory links mapped to source trees; no missing paths found
  - no proof assistant or model checker was run; “proof artifact” means source proof text exists; successful checks are attributed to repository records where available
- how to read a row
  - safety: bad outcomes never occur, such as two owners of a lock or conflicting chosen values
  - liveness: a requested good outcome eventually occurs; delivery, scheduling, quorum and failure assumptions remain part of the claim
  - deadlock freedom alone does not imply that each waiting client eventually succeeds; state-level enabledness is distinguished where identified
  - stated property, configured check, proof script, successful recorded run and complete proof are different evidence levels
  - “not found” records this inspection’s limit, not a proof of absence; imported modules can supply properties
  - size means measured physical lines, including comments/blanks; generated code is included where stated; overlapping file/directory scopes must not be summed as unique effort
  - short source quotes preserve declaration names/formulas; plain-English interpretations are agent inferences; read linked full statements before reusing assumptions
- navigation
  - [TLA+, PlusCal, TLAPS and Apalache](#tla-source-cases)
  - [TLA+ in systems and P](#industrial-specifications-and-p)
  - [Ivy, mypyvy, DuoAI, DistAI, SWISS, Veil and Quint](#invariant-and-modeling-tools)
  - [Coq/Rocq: Verdi, DiSeL, Aneris, Velisarios, Toychain and Grove/Perennial](#coq-and-rocq)
  - [Dafny and Verus: IronFleet, Anvil, IronKV, node replication, storage and concurrency examples](#dafny-and-verus)
  - [Isabelle/HOL and native Lean 4](#isabelle-and-lean)
- file coverage
  - TLA+ local suites: 365 rows; external TLA+ suites and extra proof files: 115
  - industrial TLA+/P: 74; Ivy/invariant suites/Quint: 534; Coq/Rocq: 200; Dafny/Verus: 60; Isabelle/native Lean/Cadence: 198
- online discovery and limits
  - both web-search endpoints failed (HTTP 404 or empty error); fallback used curl/Python against GitHub repository search APIs, then git clones and source inspection
  - GitHub search queries included `afp mirror`, `consensus language:Lean`, `distributed language:Lean`, `paxos language:Lean`, `raft language:Lean`, `SWISS invariant`, `DuoAI`, `DistAI`, `verified-storage`, and `distributed language:Isabelle`; API responses are retained in research_verified
  - reused the 27 supplied clones and local Verus/IronKV/node-replication trees; cloned additional source repositories as needed
  - `verus-lang/verified-storage` resolved through repository discovery to [microsoft/verified-storage](https://github.com/microsoft/verified-storage), whose source README says “This repository contains code for verified storage systems”
  - Kafka, BookKeeper and Pulsar current inspected checkouts contained no matching source specification files; this does not rule out old branches or separate repositories
  - pure mathematics, sequential data-structure exercises, compiler syntax tests and puzzles were excluded; concurrent resource protocols and crash/storage protocols remain explicitly labeled
  - papers found: 0; PDFs saved: 0 in this source-only slice; neighboring review slices collect papers separately; human effort figures were not found in the inspected source evidence

## TLA+ source cases

## TLA+, PlusCal, TLAPS and Apalache source inventory

- measurement and status convention
  - one row per `.tla` module, including proof and model-instance variants; this deliberately preserves the difference between a problem and its supporting artifacts
  - LOC is the measured number of physical source lines, including comments and generated PlusCal translations; dependent modules and model configuration files are excluded
  - property labels below quote source identifiers/formulas; `[]` means always, `<>` means eventually, and `~>` means whenever the left side holds the right side eventually holds
  - a manifest `proof` entry identifies a TLAPS proof target, not a proof run performed for this inventory; model `result` fields are repository records, not reruns
  - a TLC `PROPERTY` may be a safety/refinement formula: the formulas, rather than the keyword alone, determine the separation below
  - plain-language reading of recurring source names: `TypeOK` means state values have the intended types; `MutualExclusion` means at most one process is in its critical section; `Agreement`/`Consistency` means decisions agree; `Validity` restricts allowable decisions; `Integrity` excludes spurious/duplicate delivery; `StarvationFree` means each waiting process eventually enters; `Termination` means execution eventually ends; `Refinement`/`Implementation` means concrete runs obey the abstract specification

  - specified: DAG-based consensus
  - artifact kind: specification/proof variant; separate artifact, not automatically a distinct problem
  - tool: TLA+/PlusCal
  - size: 231 physical lines; [exact source](https://github.com/tlaplus/Examples/blob/6a7b26a31c1a6aeec789b455e9bbfa3b3ad2728f/specifications/dag-consensus/Sailfish.tla)
  - safety: `TypeOK` is the type invariant; `Agreement` says correct nodes have compatible logs; `correctNode` is a protocol action, not a property; [definitions](https://github.com/tlaplus/Examples/blob/6a7b26a31c1a6aeec789b455e9bbfa3b3ad2728f/specifications/dag-consensus/Sailfish.tla#L212)
    - source: “Agreement == \A n1,n2 \in N \ F : Compatible(log[n1], log[n2])”
  - liveness-related condition: after GST, for a round whose leader is nonfaulty, each correct node that has reached two rounds later has committed that leader vertex; [definition](https://github.com/tlaplus/Examples/blob/6a7b26a31c1a6aeec789b455e9bbfa3b3ad2728f/specifications/dag-consensus/Sailfish.tla#L227)
    - source: “Liveness == \A r \in R : r >= GST /\ Leader(r) \notin F =>”
      - next line: “    \A n \in N \ F : round[n] >= r+2 =>”
    - limitation: this named `Liveness` formula is a state predicate checked as an invariant; it does not assert that nodes eventually advance two rounds or eventually reach GST
  - evidence/status: specification/support module; no proof target or model result attached to this module in manifest; [manifest](https://github.com/tlaplus/Examples/blob/6a7b26a31c1a6aeec789b455e9bbfa3b3ad2728f/specifications/dag-consensus/manifest.json)

- added repositories discovered through the README-only references in `tlaplus/Examples`; downloaded author source files/archives are labeled separately and have stable author URLs rather than Git commit URLs

## Industrial specifications and P

TLA+ / PlusCal: industrial source specifications

- scope and measurement
  - primary modules get separate rows; model-checking configuration, trace-validation wrappers, and imported helpers stay with their underlying problem unless they define a different model
  - property names are verbatim source quotations; plain descriptions of their intent are inferences from the definitions
  - these files and configurations show intended checks, not successful reruns; no model checker or proof checker was run for this inventory
- MongoDB exploratory Raft single-member reconfiguration
  - specifies: Raft replication with original Raft single-server membership changes
  - safety: no separate property configuration found; transition/state definitions present
  - liveness: `Liveness` supplies strong/weak scheduling fairness only; no separate eventual outcome is stated
  - tool and evidence: TLA+; TLC configurations, no TLAPS proof found
  - measured size: 263 physical lines in [RaftMongoWithRaftReconfig.tla](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/0d30700a47defbf2a38dbd7bba7981ab6964b040/src/mongo/tla_plus/RaftMongoWithRaftReconfig.tla); comments and blank lines included
  - fairness premises: the operator `Liveness` restricts scheduling so enabled replication, rollback and selected write actions cannot be postponed forever; these are assumptions used to check progress, not independently proved eventual outcomes
- MongoDB Raft replication
  - source caveat: "NeverRollbackCommitted and NeverRollbackBeforeCommitPoint can be violated"; the configuration points to SERVER-39626 and says the required five-server state space is larger than easily checked
  - specifies: primary elections, oplog replication, rollback and commit-point propagation
  - safety: at most one primary per election term; committed log entries and entries before the local commit point cannot be rolled back; source: `NoTwoPrimariesInSameTerm`, `NeverRollbackCommitted`, `NeverRollbackBeforeCommitPoint`
  - liveness: nodes with different commit points eventually agree after rollback stops; source: `CommitPointEventuallyPropagates`
  - tool and evidence: TLA+; TLC configurations, no TLAPS proof found
  - measured size: 331 physical lines in [RaftMongo.tla](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/0d30700a47defbf2a38dbd7bba7981ab6964b040/src/mongo/tla_plus/Replication/RaftMongo/RaftMongo.tla); comments and blank lines included; [MCRaftMongo.cfg](https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/0d30700a47defbf2a38dbd7bba7981ab6964b040/src/mongo/tla_plus/Replication/RaftMongo/MCRaftMongo.cfg) states the enabled checks
  - fairness premises: the operator `Liveness` restricts scheduling so enabled replication, rollback and selected write actions cannot be postponed forever; these are assumptions used to check progress, not independently proved eventual outcomes
- MongoDB Raft replication timestamps
  - specifies: replication with persistence, application, restart and failover
  - safety: at most one primary per term; committed entries and the committed storage snapshot must survive rollback; source: `NoTwoPrimariesInSameTerm`, `NeverRollbackCommitted`, `NeverRollbackBeforeCommitPoint`, `CommittedSnapshotNeverRollback`
  - liveness: commit-point agreement is the intended target, but its check is disabled; source: `CommitPointEventuallyPropagates` is commented out; fairness remains in `Liveness`

P: tutorials, proof examples and protocol benchmarks

- evidence rules
  - repository tutorial states: "we will rely on proofs by induction"; the same introduction names "UCLID5 and Z3" ([P verification tutorial](https://github.com/p-org/P/blob/260da928f67569ca7a8c0039a02d0bad7cde6096/Docs/docs/advanced/PVerifierLanguageExtensions/twophasecommitverification.md#L3))
  - portfolio README: "This folder contains P model checking problems for well-known distributed protocols" ([source](https://github.com/p-org/P/blob/260da928f67569ca7a8c0039a02d0bad7cde6096/Tst/PortfolioTests/README.md#L1)); it counts 12 Paxos and 8 two-phase-commit problems, but this inventory counts source model variants rather than test parameter settings
  - `Proof` blocks are proof artifacts; this inventory did not execute the verifier, so successful machine checking is unconfirmed
  - `hot state` marks a progress monitor; ordinary assertions and invariants are safety obligations
  - portfolio models without assertions remain useful protocol inputs, but do not establish a stated guarantee

## Invariant and modeling tools

- scope: one row per source specification/encoding; variants and deliberately buggy models stay separate, so row count is not a count of distinct algorithms
  - size: physical lines, including comments/blanks, of the linked file; excludes imported dependencies unless separately stated
  - evidence: source declarations and proof/checking commands inspected; verification was not executed
  - safety/liveness labels identify stated or attempted targets, not established guarantees; every filename marked bad/buggy/unsafe/error/err/warn has a negative-test warning
  - plain-language readings are inferences from the full nearby formulas; fairness/specification premises and explicitly false targets are separated from intended progress targets
  - property labels below are the repository authors’ names; a state invariant states safety; formulas that contain eventuality state progress, sometimes under fairness assumptions
  - when a row says no declaration found, the protocol may import its contract from another module
  - names describing the system are inferred from filenames and source declarations; linked code is the primary evidence

- Veil proof boundary: [README](https://github.com/verse-lab/veil/blob/626901534a8c788e45b350328021cd4d7a942c32/README.md#L8) says “proving safety (and, in the future, liveness)”
  - [Base.lean](https://github.com/verse-lab/veil/blob/626901534a8c788e45b350328021cd4d7a942c32/Veil/Base.lean#L144) declares `veil.smt.trust` with `defValue := true` and explains: “If false, `veil_smt` asks the SMT backend to reconstruct Lean proofs.”
  - `#check_invariants` with the default setting is SMT-backed invariant checking; native Lean theorem text is identified separately; no completed Lean-kernel check is claimed here
- SWISS [benchmark README](https://github.com/secure-foundations/SWISS/blob/348b9c4f9b0b2f124b50c8f420d071f4bc0789b3/benchmarks/README.md#L8) says: “the other one was translated by hand.”; `.ivy` and `.pyv` rows are alternative source encodings

- coverage and gaps
  - Ivy scan includes protocol examples, liveness examples, TileLink coherence examples, protocol tutorials/testing variants, QUIC contract modules and selected protocol regression models
  - excludes Ivy language/compiler tests, sequential collection implementations, CPU pipeline/ALU examples, generic tactic tests and puzzle examples; accompanying libraries and harnesses may hold extra contracts
  - mypyvy scan includes protocol encodings, unsafe variants, prophecy/relaxation benchmark variants; excludes unrelated sequential structures and language regressions
  - DuoAI and DistAI: all `.ivy` files under `protocols`; DistAI matching generated outputs linked where present
  - SWISS: every `.ivy`/`.pyv` benchmark file; paired encodings deliberately remain separate
  - Veil: every non-puzzle `Examples/**/*.lean` file except `SCPTheory.lean`, which is a supporting quorum theory rather than a transition-system case
  - Quint: every classic distributed `.qnt`, Cosmos consensus/IBC/light-client/bank core model, and every CometBFT `.qnt`; support modules remain separate when they specify subsystem behavior
  - checks were not executed; no successful proof/model-checking result inferred solely from a property or command declaration
  - quoted declaration excerpts are source locators; multi-line formulas and imported assumptions must be read at those links before reusing a case as an evaluation task
  - temporal safety declarations without eventuality are listed under safety; named temporal specifications/fairness assumptions are kept under liveness when they include progress but are not necessarily standalone guarantees

## Coq and Rocq

- measurement and evidence rules
  - LOC counts physical lines, including comments and blank lines, in the named `.v` file(s) or recursive directory; shared framework dependencies are excluded
  - every link pins the inspected commit; repository source and proof scripts were inspected, but Coq/Rocq builds were not run
  - “proof scripts” means proof artifacts are present, not that this survey independently checked them; admitted statements and commented drafts are identified locally, without a whole dependency audit
  - liveness is recorded only for explicit eventual/progress statements; ordinary partial-correctness Hoare triples do not establish eventual return

## Dafny and Verus

Rows distinguish source proof artifacts from fresh verification runs. Counts are mechanically computed from tracked files at the linked commits. Component rows overlap system rows; do not sum their sizes. “No liveness theorem found” means inspection did not locate one, not a proof that none exists. Storage rows are explicitly adjacent crash protocols, rather than multi-node distributed algorithms.

- Dafny / IronFleet
  - IronLock
    - Specifies: a distributed token/lock transferred between hosts
    - Safety: refines one serial history of lock holders
    - Liveness: no liveness theorem found in this service
    - Tool/result: Dafny theorem proof artifact; proof sources inspected, checker not rerun here

- Coverage and gaps
  - 60 rows; public sources and local clones inspected; no PDFs downloaded in this repository-focused slice
  - `verus-lang/verified-storage` did not exist at lookup; GitHub repository search located `microsoft/verified-storage`, whose README says “This repository contains code for verified storage systems” ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/verified-storage/blob/41cab95051229ebd457b4eed7fc111e3e7c9099c/README.md))
  - Anvil main omits the old ZooKeeper/FluentBit examples; the OSDI24 artifact commit retains them and was inspected separately
  - IronRSL Counter and KV C# application wrappers are examples atop the verified replication library; not counted as independently proved protocols: README says “IronRSL-Counter and IronRSL-KV are examples showing how to write a service in C#” ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/Ironclad/blob/2fe4dcdc323b92e93f759cc3e373521366b7f691/ironfleet/README.md)); CODE.md labels their clients “Unverified C# client”
  - Generic arithmetic/ADT Verus examples, unverified tutorial variants, topological sort, and primitive-cell syntax demos are outside concurrent/distributed-protocol scope
  - Ghost resource APIs are listed separately because they specify shared authority, not a network implementation
  - PoWER API soundness arguments are verification-method proofs rather than a concrete protocol case, so the storage rows do not count them separately
  - Proof presence does not establish that every declaration is proved: platform/network/crash models and explicit assumptions remain trusted; ARC/Rc overflow assumptions and ignored experimental examples are marked in their rows
